snippet: St. Petersburg has pivoted its medical services market, replacing European patient flows with demand from the CIS, Asia, and the Middle East. The city now functions as a hub for complex pathologies, leveraging a high density of federal centers and specialized scientific schools rather than isolated technologies. The shift in geography is stark. Western patients have been replaced by citizens of Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Azerbaijan, Armenia, and Turkmenistan. Growth from Asia is more aggressive: by 2024, patient flows from India rose by 274% and from China by 32%, while Iran and Egypt emerged as steady sources of patients in 2025-2026. Demand concentrates in oncology, neurosurgery, transplantology, reproductive medicine, and ophthalmology. In oncology, the city's competitive edge is the ability to provide a complete treatment path for complex cases within a single urban footprint.

headline: Mushroom and Mozzarella Salad with Pesto Dressing
snippet: Mozzarella is delicate. It melts quickly. If you add hot mushrooms to the salad, the cheese turns into a puddle and the arugula goes limp. The whole trick is timing. Sear the mushrooms. Let them cool. Then assemble. The contrast between the warm earthiness of the fungi and the cool, creamy bite of the cheese is what makes this dish work. Without that pause, you get a warm mush, not a salad. Ingredients (for 4 servings) 200 g fresh mushrooms 200 g tomatoes 100 g mini-mozzarella balls 70 g mixed greens with arugula 50 g red onion 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil 1.5 tbsp pesto sauce ¼ lemon Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste Method Wipe the mushrooms clean with a damp cloth and slice them in half. Heat one tablespoon of olive oil in a skillet over high heat. Spread the mushrooms in a single layer. Sear for about four minutes until the edges are browned, tossing them occasionally. Season with salt at the end. Moment of truth: Transfer the mushrooms to a flat plate. Leave them at room temperature for five to seven minutes. This pause is non-negotiable if you want the cheese to hold its shape and the leaves to stay crisp.

headline: Rival Systems Targets Cross-Asset Traders with FX Expansion
snippet: Rival Systems, a Chicago-based provider of trading and risk management solutions, added spot FX and FX forwards to its multi-asset trading system Rival One. London's trading industry is coming home! The new offering extends the platform’s product set, which already includes futures, options, equities and crypto, enabling professional traders to implement complex trading and risk management strategies. FX Joins Existing Trading Infrastructure Rival One brings OTC spot FX and forwards into the same workflow as its existing markets. The new instruments use common trading infrastructure, risk controls and APIs, with order management, real-time positions and market data available across supported products. The platform connects to multiple FX brokers , allowing clients to use their preferred brokerage and liquidity providers. Post-trade exposure can be managed through Rival Risk, the company’s separate enterprise risk management platform, which already supports FX alongside equities, futures and other products. Rival One is a fully hosted, cloud-based order and execution management system. Its existing functionality includes smart order routing, basket trading, post-trade allocation and tools for trading spreads across asset classes and exchanges. A Common Workflow for Professional Trading Desks The platform targets professional traders running systematic and discretionary strategies. Its allocation tools also support asset managers, commodity trading advisers and other firms managing multiple accounts. For desks trading both exchange-traded and OTC instruments , the expansion brings currency execution into their existing trading environment. “Rival One has always been about bringing different markets together in one trading environment,” said Rob D’Arco, CEO of Rival Systems. “Adding spot FX and forwards expands that capability even further. Our clients can now trade across six major asset classes without having to move between different systems.” Partners can also use Rival’s order management system to integrate multi-asset trading into their proprietary platforms, extending access beyond Rival One’s own interface. TT and FlexFX Offer Broader FX Workflows Trading Technologies published FX coverage includes non-deliverable forwards and swaps in addition to spot and forwards. It combines OTC FX with futures and precious metals, offering streaming execution, requests for quotes and requests for streams. FlexFX focuses on broker-neutral liquidity aggregation and execution, combining prices from banks, non-bank providers and electronic communication networks. It supports broker algorithms, voice transactions and execution analytics. Dealer tools also let traders negotiate forward points and convert voice trades into electronic records. Rival’s announcement establishes support for spot and forwards through multiple brokers, but does not name those connections or specify the currency pairs and forward tenors available. headline: Thani bin Abdullah Foundation, QU sign cooperation agreement
snippet:
Doha, Qatar: Qatar University (QU) signs a cooperation agreement with Thani bin Abdullah Foundation for Humanitarian Services to enhance student support and strengthen collaboration in training, community engagement, and volunteer initiatives.

The agreement was signed by Vice President for Student Affairs at QU, Dr. Mohammad Diab, and  CEO of the Thani Bin Abdullah Foundation for Humanitarian Services, Dr. Ayed bin Dabsan Al-Qahtani, in the presence of officials from both parties.

The agreement establishes an institutional framework for cooperation in providing financial assistance to QU students, implementing community service and awareness programmes, and organising conferences, workshops, and training courses aimed at developing skills and building capacity.

Commenting on the agreement, Vice President for Student Affairs at QU, Dr. Mohammad Diab, said, “This agreement reflects QU’s commitment to strengthening student support, developing students’ skills, and expanding opportunities for their active participation in community service, while fostering a stronger sense of social responsibility.”

For his part, CEO of the Thani Bin Abdullah Foundation for Humanitarian Services, Dr. Ayed bin Dabsan Al-Qahtani, said, “This agreement reaffirms Thani Humanitarian Foundation’s commitment to supporting our students and enhancing their educational and community engagement opportunities. It also reflects our strong belief in the importance of partnership and cooperation among national institutions in this field, helping students continue their educational journey and further develop their capabilities.”

Dr. Ayed Al-Qahtani added, “Through our cooperation with Qatar University, we are keen to expand the scope of our joint efforts to include providing financial support services to students, implementing training, capacity-building and awareness programmes, and promoting a culture of volunteerism and community service.”

He continued, “We believe that integration and collaboration among educational, humanitarian and community institutions contribute to creating sustainable impact and pave the way for further initiatives that serve students and strengthen their engagement in society. We look forward to this agreement providing an effective framework for advancing cooperation between the Foundation and Qatar University, particularly as the national university represents the largest community of higher education students in Qatar. This encourages us to further our efforts and contributions toward providing our students with an outstanding educational environment.”
